The *Corīvuṭṭhāpikā* ("Ordaining a criminal") is the second training rule in the *Saṅghādisesa* class of the Pali *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga* [SuttaCentral]. The rule stipulates that a Buddhist nun who ordains a female criminal who has been sentenced to death incurs an offense entailing temporary suspension (*saṅghādisesa*) [SuttaCentral]. In modern scholarship and digital repositories, it is available in English translation by Bhikkhu Brahmali on SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral].

This disciplinary rule is preserved across all major extant Vinaya traditions [SuttaCentral]. Parallel enactments and vibhaṅga expositions are found within the Pali *Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha* (Ss 2) and *Bhikkhunī Parivāra* (Ss 2), the Dharmaguptaka Vinaya (Ss 5), the Mahīśāsaka Vinaya (Ss 4), the Sarvāstivāda Vinaya (Ss 8) and its Sanskrit Prātimokṣa fragments, the Mūlasarvāstivāda Vinaya in both Chinese (Ss 10) and Tibetan (Ss 10) translations, the Mahāsāṅghika Vinaya (Ss 8), and the Lokottaravāda Sanskrit *Bhikṣuṇīvinaya* (Ss 8) [SuttaCentral].
